title: Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD)
seo_title: Grade 8 Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD) Worksheets (TEKS 8.11B, STAAR)
standard_text: 8.11B determine the mean absolute deviation and use this quantity as a measure of the average distance data are from the mean using a data set of no more than 10 data points
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 mean absolute deviation worksheets for Texas TEKS 8.11B: find the mean and MAD step by step, compare spread and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: MAD = average distance from the mean.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The mean absolute deviation (MAD) is the average distance of the data from the mean.
  • Step 1: find the mean. Step 2: find each value's distance from the mean (always positive). Step 3: average the distances.
  • A small MAD means the data are close to the mean; a large MAD means they are spread out.

Examples

Example

3, 5, 7, 9

Mean = 6

Distances 3, 1, 1, 3

8 ÷ 4

Answer: MAD = 2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Keeping negative distancesDistances are absolute values; without them the sum is 0.
Dividing by the wrong countDivide by the number of values.
Thinking a bigger mean means a bigger MADMAD measures spread, not size.

faq.a: Determine the mean absolute deviation and use this quantity as a measure of the average distance data are from the mean using a data set of no more than 10 data points.
Yes, when every value equals the mean.

faq.q: Is MAD the same as range?
faq.a: No. Range uses only the max and min; MAD uses every value.
Distances above and below the mean would cancel out otherwise.
